traces.question: The claim under test is that the particles become rough-shelled core-shell hybrids, growing from about 70 nm to 95-100 nm. Given the SEM panels F3a and F3e, do they confirm that Ag has deposited as a discrete shell on the BST core?
traces.answer_key: No item can be scored here. The panel audit itself finds no discrete Ag nanoparticles resolved on any BST@Ag surface: the SEM panels show only surface roughening, and the unmodified BST panel already carries bright particles of similar size, so SEM cannot distinguish a genuine Ag shell from the base particle's own texture (a1). But this does not settle the claim either way, because the claim is independently carried by a floor-level observation outside the SEM channel: the powders visibly darken from white (BST-SH) through pale yellow, tan and brown as Ag loading rises (u5), which tracks Ag content without needing the SEM feature to be resolved. Since the claim reaches support through this non-panel route regardless of what the SEM audit shows, the panel question has no decisive answer to grade.
traces.grading: Closed: the audit ruling on panel a1 is inconclusive by design (SEM cannot resolve the feature), and the floor mechanism already reaches the claim through u5 without needing that SEM/feature-matching evidence, so there is no pass/fail item left to test against the panel. Confirmed against nodes a1 (audit ruling) and u5 (floor support) in the record's own floor field.

Ruling: It is the 1% film, not the 5%, whose loss runs away above 200 kHz, reaching 0.065 at 1 MHz

traces.question: The text claims dielectric loss stays at or below 0.038 at 100 Hz and falls to about 0.013 above 100 kHz for the 3 and 5% films. Does the panel (F6b) bear this out?
traces.answer_key: No. The panel shows the opposite pattern from what the claim describes: it is the 1% film, not the 5%, whose loss runs away above 200 kHz, climbing to 0.065 at 1 MHz (a3).
traces.grading: Answer key: the audit ruling on the panel (a3).
